purpose: Defines the commercial and lifecycle structure that hangs off each asset identity: ownership, CAPEX reference, warranty, replacement cost, service life, spare parts and end of life. The design package contains no prices, dates, serial numbers or warranty records, so this document imports nothing. Its value is that the shape exists and the gaps are explicit.

import_instructions.summary: Every monetary and date field below is null and every data_status is not_yet_imported. A human must supply the real records; nothing here may be filled in by inference.
required_from_the_owner: A CAPEX reference for each purchased asset: purchase order, invoice number or accounting line item.
Acquisition cost and currency, and the purchase date, from the invoice rather than from memory.
The in-service date, which is often months after the purchase date and drives warranty and depreciation.
Serial number or asset tag, recorded as an external identifier on the asset, not as its canonical ID.
Warranty terms, warranty start basis and expiry date, including any extended coverage purchased later.
Current replacement cost, refreshed periodically, since replacement cost is not acquisition cost.
Expected service life in years, with the basis: manufacturer statement, insurer requirement or policy.
Spare-parts holdings for each asset: part identity, quantity on hand, storage location and reorder point.
End-of-life and disposal expectations for anything containing batteries, refrigerant or hazardous material.
import_rules: Set data_status to imported on a record only when every field on that record has been supplied or explicitly marked not applicable. Partial imports keep data_status at partially_imported.
Correct ownership_state by hand where it is wrong. The derived value comes from register status alone and register status is a design-progress field, not a proof of possession.
Never write a price, date or serial number into this document that is not copied from a real record.

Physical replacement does not create a new lifecycle record for the functional position (SDD rule 25.3.6). The replacement equipment gets its own asset and its own lifecycle record, linked by a replaces relationship.
Spare parts are recorded as a list of holdings against the asset that consumes them, not as assets.
known_blockers: The energy capacity revision is unresolved, so no PV, inverter or battery CAPEX figure can be correct yet. See docs/design-decisions/DD-001-energy-capacity-revision.md.
The property has not been confirmed, so land, site works, well drilling and trenching have no scope.
Generator, battery chemistry, controller family and historian are all unselected, so their CAPEX lines do not exist.

ownership_derivation.rule: ownership_state is derived from the register status field and from nothing else. No source document in this package asserts possession of any equipment, so no record is marked owned on any other basis.
ownership_derivation.observed_result: No asset in the v0.3 register carries a status of procured, installed, commissioned or active. Only the two reserve-status records derive to owned. The source material describes some rack hardware as existing, but the register does not record that, and this document will not add it.

field_semantics.ownership_state: owned, planned, leased or unknown. Derived; correct it by hand on import.
field_semantics.acquisition_status: Whether a purchase record exists to import.
field_semantics.capex_reference: Accounting handle for the purchase. Null until imported.
field_semantics.in_service_date: Date the asset began operating. Drives warranty and depreciation. Null until imported.
field_semantics.warranty_status: not_yet_imported, active, expired, void or not_applicable.
field_semantics.replacement_cost_status: Replacement cost is what it costs to replace today, not what was paid.
field_semantics.expected_service_life_years: Planning life for renewal budgeting. Null until an owner or vendor states it.
field_semantics.spare_parts: Holdings that serve this asset: part identity, quantity, location, reorder point.
field_semantics.spares_policy_required: Derived from register criticality: critical and life-safety assets need a decision.

coverage.extension_assets_not_covered: Water extension assets in data/water_assets.yaml are all status concept and receive lifecycle records when that extension is merged into the base register.

notes: The property itself. Acquisition of land is a CAPEX line of its own and precedes every other record here.

This document contains no price, no date, no serial number and no warranty term. That is the point of it.
A record whose data_status is not_yet_imported must not be used for insurance valuation, depreciation, renewal budgeting or procurement planning.

Register status answers 'where is this in the design', not 'do we own it'. The two are being conflated here only because the register is the only evidence available, and the derivation is stated so it can be audited and corrected.
